name: e08_multi_asset_portfolio
title: 8. Trend as a portfolio: ten markets instead of one stock
text:
**Question.** What does EMA50/200 trend following look like as a diversified multi-asset portfolio, and what does it add to a 60/40 investor?

**Setup.** One long/cash sleeve per CORE ETF (SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, EEM, IEF, TLT, GLD, DBC, VNQ), inverse 63-day-vol weights reset monthly, next-close fills, 5 bp costs, cash in T-bills; benchmarks are monthly-rebalanced 60/40 SPY/IEF, equal-weight CORE and SPY, plus a control that holds the same inverse-vol book always long. Common window 2004-05-28 to 2026-10-28; EEM, GLD, VNQ and DBC join the static benchmarks once they trade and the trend, TSMOM and control books once their EMA50/200 signal is warm, so the three inverse-vol books always hold the same set of markets.

**Findings.**

- **Headline:** the trend book returns 6.0% a year at 7.0% vol (Sharpe 0.60, max drawdown −15%) vs 8.2% at 10.5% for 60/40 (Sharpe 0.62, −33%). It trails 60/40 on Sharpe by 0.02 (95% CI −0.35 to 0.32). Scaled to a 10% vol target (10.1% realised, 1.14x average gross exposure) it earns 7.7% with a −17% max drawdown, so the drawdown gap survives at matched risk. TSMOM 12M sleeves give Sharpe 0.65.
- **Diversification vs signal:** the ten single-asset EMA sleeves average a Sharpe of 0.32 (9 of 10 below the portfolio's 0.60; best QQQ, 0.69). But the *same* inverse-vol book held permanently long has Sharpe 0.62 (trend minus it: −0.01, 95% CI −0.27 to 0.26) and a −25% max drawdown.
- **Correlation and worst months:** monthly ρ = 0.61 to SPY and 0.67 to 60/40; beta to 60/40 is 0.29 in 60/40's down months and 0.30 in its up months. In 60/40's ten worst months (average −6.4%) the trend book averaged −1.8% and was never positive.
- **Stress years:** 2008 trend 7.2% vs 60/40 −18.0%; 2020 trend 0.7% vs 60/40 16.0%; 2022 trend −3.9% vs 60/40 −16.7%. In 2008 the Treasury sleeves contributed +11.0% and the equity sleeves −4.1%. In 2022 SPY returned −18.2% and IEF −15.2%; the trend book's equity and REIT sleeves contributed −6.4% (−4.2% in January-March and −2.2% after, until the last sleeves (SPY, VNQ) exited in May), T-bills +1.8% and commodities +1.1%.
- **Blend:** 80% 60/40 + 20% trend moves Sharpe 0.62 → 0.65 (one-sided p = 0.12), max drawdown −33% → −26%, CAGR 8.2% → 7.7%.

**Interpretation.** Combining ten sleeves roughly doubles the typical sleeve's Sharpe (0.32 → 0.60): the diversification effect behind Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) and Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017), and what the single-asset NVDA framing missed. The uncomfortable part is that diversification does the same for buy-and-hold (0.36 → 0.62), largely via the inverse-vol tilt to Treasuries (36% of the passive book; monthly ρ(SPY, IEF) = −0.07), so here the EMA signal adds no Sharpe. What it adds is drawdown control at matched risk: −17% for the vol-targeted book vs −25% for the passive one. Down-month beta to 60/40 (0.29) is no lower than up-month beta (0.30): the cushioning in bad months reflects low beta and a large cash and bond allocation, not the convex payoff Fung & Hsieh (2001) describe for long/short trend followers. In 2022, when the bond leg of 60/40 failed as a hedge, the book was on average only 23% invested and lost 3.9% instead of 16.7%; being long/cash it could only step aside, not profit from shorts as long/short managed-futures programmes can (not modelled here). 2020 is the failure mode: after the fast COVID crash (March −6.8%, the book's worst month) equity/REIT exposure fell from 55% to 6% and was back only to 38% by December, so April-December returned 11.3% vs 26.3% for 60/40. A 20% sleeve raises 60/40's Sharpe by 0.03 (not significant, p = 0.12) and cuts its drawdown for 0.4 pp of CAGR: a diversifier trade-off, not a free lunch.
after: All benchmarks and the trend book are evaluated on the same dates. The 2x-capped vol-targeted variant borrows at the T-bill rate, which flatters it. Calendar-year cells in the stress table show return (max drawdown within the year). Single-sleeve Sharpe ratios start at each sleeve's own warm-up date (the From column). The inverse-vol control and the TSMOM book add each sleeve on the bar its EMA50/200 signal warms up (461 bars after listing), although always-long and TSMOM signals would be available earlier. Stress-year attributions sum daily contributions and are approximate. p-values are one-sided (paired stationary bootstrap, H0: no improvement).
